To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The errors on the experimental inputs to the parton analysis have been underestimated by about a factor 2.5, 2) the uncertainties on the partons are correspondingly larger than previously estimated and 3) the errors on physical observables can be calculated reliably.

the uncertainties on the partons and the physical observables can be determined reliably, and that the uncertainties on physical observables are dominated by the experimental uncertainties on the data.

the uncertainties in predictions from parton densities are dominated by errors on the experimental input, that these errors can be reliably estimated and that the errors are typically of the order of the central value, with a few exceptions where they are larger.
In summary, our research is concerned with
uncertainties of predictions from partons.

the propagation of errors in the parton distributions, and the uncertainties on predictions for physical quantities that result from the experimental data that enter into the determination of those distributions.
the determination of the uncertainties on the partons and predictions for physical quantities arising from the uncertainties in the experimental data used in the global parton analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, although the uncertainties on the experimental data used in the global analysis are not negligible, they can be propagated in a reliable way using the linear method, and the resulting uncertainties are small enough for many purposes.
, in the case of the MRST2001 analysis, the experimental uncertainties are by far the dominant ones.
the uncertainties in parton distributions are not yet fully under theoretical control and that the experimental errors are not yet small enough to allow the use of linear error propagation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the errors on the parton distribution functions, which are the most important source of uncertainty in theoretical predictions, have been determined with reasonable accuracy.

, in the case of the MRST2001 fit, the uncertainties from the experimental errors on the data are the dominant contribution to the overall uncertainty on physical quantities, and the uncertainties from the fitting procedure are of secondary importance.
the uncertainties on the partons, and on the predictions from them, are significantly reduced when using the MRST2001 analysis as compared to the MRST1998 analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
uncertainties on predictions from parton distribution fits can be determined in a straightforward way, and that the uncertainties can be very substantial.
the uncertainties in predictions of physical quantities are dominated by those in the experimental data, not those in the fit procedure.
, in order to determine the uncertainties on any observable, the errors on the parton distribution functions should be calculated by diagonalizing the error covariance matrix.
